title: Born in Duluth, Minnesota
note: Robert Allen Zimmerman spent most of his childhood in Hibbing.

title: Moves to New York
note: Dylan enters the Greenwich Village folk scene.

title: Debut recording sessions
note: John Hammond produces the two Columbia sessions that become Dylan’s first album.

title: March on Washington
note: Dylan and Joan Baez perform at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom.

title: An electric set at Newport
note: Dylan takes the Newport Folk Festival stage with an electric band.

title: Tarantula appears in print
note: Macmillan publishes Dylan’s book of prose and poetry.

title: Concert for Bangladesh
note: Dylan joins George Harrison’s benefit at Madison Square Garden.

title: Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid
note: Dylan plays Alias in Sam Peckinpah’s western and writes music for the film.

title: The Last Waltz
note: Dylan takes part in the Band’s farewell concert at Winterland in San Francisco.

title: First Grammy
note: “Gotta Serve Somebody” wins Best Rock Vocal Performance, Male.

title: Live Aid
note: Dylan plays the Philadelphia benefit with Keith Richards and Ronnie Wood.

title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame
note: Bruce Springsteen inducts Dylan into the Hall of Fame.

title: The Traveling Wilburys
note: Dylan records Vol. 1 with George Harrison, Jeff Lynne, Roy Orbison and Tom Petty.

title: Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award
note: The Recording Academy honors Dylan’s body of work.

title: Thirty years of recordings
note: Musicians gather at Madison Square Garden to celebrate three decades since Dylan’s debut.

title: Time Out of Mind wins Album of the Year
note: The Recording Academy names Dylan’s album its Album of the Year.

title: Golden Globe for “Things Have Changed”
note: The song from Wonder Boys wins Best Original Song.

title: Academy Award for “Things Have Changed”
note: Dylan wins the Oscar for Original Song for Wonder Boys.

title: Masked and Anonymous
note: Dylan plays musician Jack Fate and co-writes the film with director Larry Charles.

title: Chronicles: Volume One
note: Dylan publishes his memoir, moving between Greenwich Village and the recording studio.

title: No Direction Home
note: Martin Scorsese’s documentary revisits Dylan’s early years and his electric tours.

title: Theme Time Radio Hour
note: Dylan begins hosting a radio show built around a different theme each episode.

title: The Drawn Blank Series
note: The Kunstsammlungen Chemnitz exhibits Dylan’s visual art.

title: Pulitzer special citation
note: The Pulitzer Board recognizes Dylan’s impact on popular music and American culture.

title: Presidential Medal of Freedom
note: President Barack Obama presents Dylan with the medal at the White House.

title: Légion d’honneur
note: France honors Dylan at a ceremony in Paris.

title: MusiCares Person of the Year
note: The Recording Academy’s charitable foundation honors Dylan.

title: The archive comes to Tulsa
note: The acquisition brings manuscripts, recordings and other materials to Oklahoma.

title: Nobel Prize in Literature
note: The Swedish Academy announces Dylan as the literature laureate.

title: Nobel lecture
note: Dylan’s recorded lecture traces the connections between songs and the books he read.

title: Publishing catalogue acquisition
note: Universal Music Publishing Group announces its acquisition of Dylan’s songwriting catalogue.

title: Recorded music catalogue acquisition
note: Sony Music announces its purchase of Dylan’s recorded music catalogue.

title: Bob Dylan Center opens
note: The Tulsa museum opens its doors to the public.

title: The Philosophy of Modern Song
note: Dylan publishes a book of essays on recordings by other artists.

title: A Complete Unknown
note: James Mangold’s film about Dylan’s early career opens in US theaters.

title: Point Blank (Quick Studies)
note: Drawings from 2021 and 2022 appear in a new book of Dylan’s artwork.

title: Marries Sara Lownds
note: Dylan and Lownds marry during the year of his electric breakthrough.

title: Motorcycle accident near Woodstock
note: Dylan withdraws from touring after the crash in upstate New York.

title: The Basement Tapes sessions
note: Dylan and members of the future Band record together around Woodstock.

title: Back on tour with the Band
note: The tour opens at Chicago Stadium.

title: Rolling Thunder Revue opens
note: The ensemble plays its opening show in Plymouth, Massachusetts.

title: A new touring chapter
note: Dylan plays the Concord Pavilion in California at the start of the run often called the Never Ending Tour.

title: Kennedy Center Honors
note: Dylan is among the artists honored in Washington, DC.

title: National Medal of Arts
note: Dylan is named to the 2009 class of National Medal of Arts recipients.
